claims.text: As-synthesized equimolar WTaTiVZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
WTaTiVZr has greater multielement-induced lattice distortion than commercially pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr impedes the formation of large dislocation pile-ups.
Suppressing dislocation pile-ups decreases localized stress concentrations at grain boundaries.
Lattice distortion and suppressed pile-ups promote more spatially uniform dislocation nucleation.
Lattice distortion and suppressed pile-ups promote more uniform dislocation motion.
More uniform dislocation activity delays crack initiation.
Multielement-induced lattice distortion increases resistance to dislocation glide in WTaTiVZr.
Diminishing local dislocation pile-ups reduces catastrophic crack initiation.
Pure tungsten has more facile dislocation motion than WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
More facile dislocation motion in pure tungsten produces concentrated stress fields and early crack propagation.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will have more uniform dislocation activity and fewer dislocation pile-ups than deformed pure tungsten.
Crack initiation and propagation will be delayed in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten has limited high-temperature ductility because of localized dislocation pile-ups and brittle crack propagation.
The proposed lattice-distortion benefit applies in high-temperature plasma-facing-component service regimes.
The proposed benefit may diminish at lower temperatures because dislocation mobility is reduced in both materials.
Significant grain-size differences could invalidate the proposed comparison by changing pile-up behavior and local stresses.
Secondary-phase precipitation could diminish or obscure the proposed single-phase lattice-distortion benefit.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says lattice distortion promotes dislocation motion, while the mechanism says it increases resistance to dislocation glide. These can coexist only if the distinction between spatially distributed activation and reduced glide mobility is explicitly explained, which it is not.
